words_and_claims_to_avoid: Unsubstantiated 'top-rated', 'award-winning', '#1', 'best' (GOLD-002, GOLD-015) unless the rating/award is real, current and named (FTC Act s.5).
'Guaranteed price' or 'no hidden fees' unless the estimate is actually binding and the terms match 49 CFR 375.403.
'Fully insured' or 'full value protection included' unless true; liability options must match the released-rates notice.
'Most popular in New York' style claims (GOLD-018) without data.
'Fast, affordable and safe' as an unqualified promise; 'safe' for goods implies a guarantee.
Bundle price tables ('2BR $695', GOLD-018) without stating hours, crew size, what's included and limits.
'Moving is the most stressful life event' as a fact (not supported by Holmes & Rahe).
compliance_notes: Interstate household goods movers: every advertisement must show the name on the DOT registration and the number in the exact form 'U.S. DOT No. [number]' (49 CFR 375.207). Ads must be 'truthful, straightforward, and honest'.

Household goods BROKERS must show physical address, U.S. DOT number and MC number, and state that they are a broker that will not transport the goods and will arrange an FMCSA-authorized carrier (49 CFR 371.107).

Estimates (interstate): a physical survey is required (on-site or live/recorded video) unless the shipper waives it in writing; written binding or non-binding estimate; non-binding estimates must be free, and the shipper can't be made to pay more than 110% at delivery (49 CFR 375.401/.405). So 'free estimate' is accurate for non-binding; a mover MAY charge for a binding estimate, so 'free binding estimate' must be true.

California intrastate movers: need a Bureau of Household Goods and Services permit; advertising without one is unlawful (BPC 19237). The permit number in 'CAL-T' form is expected in ads (BHGS Max 4 tariff; CPUC has cited carriers for omitting it). Other states license intrastate movers separately: client must confirm their state rule.
'Free boxes' / 'free packing materials' (GOLD-002, 004, 008, 014): FTC Free Guide applies; state conditions next to the offer (16 CFR 251).

Self-storage 'first month free' / '$1 first month' (GOLD-012, 013, 017): show the regular monthly rate, admin fees, insurance/protection-plan requirements and any minimum stay next to the offer. Lien/auction terms are state law (self-service storage lien acts); don't advertise 'no lien' type claims.
Referral rewards (GOLD-012 '1 month free for referrals'): real terms; reviews or testimonials obtained via incentives must disclose the incentive (16 CFR 255).
Price comparisons ('save $500') must be off a real price actually charged (FTC deceptive pricing guides, 16 CFR 233).
In-home sales of moving supplies or storage contracts at the home: FTC Cooling-Off Rule may apply (16 CFR 429).
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, status, relief, nostalgia are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle and combo carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency/vendor-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.
No age/demographic angle unless a cited source supports it for this industry; even then, check Fair Housing / ECOA before using it in housing or credit.

emotion_by_offer.why: Moving is a big, uncertain bill; a concrete $ off shrinks it. Gold: $50 off local (GOLD-007/008/016), up to $500 off (GOLD-003), $100 off $1,000+ (GOLD-014).

'Up to $[X] off' only with the tiers stated
emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: Crew loading a branded truck; the family relaxed in the background.
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: 'Up to' with no tiers; dense service lists (GOLD-010/011); stock AI-looking movers (GOLD-019-022).

emotion_by_offer.why: Fear of a surprise bill or hostage load is documented by FMCSA; a written estimate after a real survey is the antidote. Nearly every gold card carries 'FREE estimate'.

emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: 'Instant quote' with no survey (implies sight-unseen pricing, the classic rogue-mover pattern); 'guaranteed price' on a non-binding estimate.

compliance_flags: Deadline must be real; don't re-run 'ends soon' indefinitely (FTC s.5).
Bertrand et al. (2010) found longer deadlines didn't hurt take-up in loan mail; test 2 vs 6 weeks.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-002 'TOP-RATED' and GOLD-015 'Award-Winning' vs FTC substantiation
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: name the real rating source/award and date, or drop it and sell the outcome.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Vendor 'instant quote / call now for a price' (GOLD-005, 019-022) vs FMCSA estimate rules and rogue-mover warnings
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins for interstate: a rate quote is not an estimate; lead with a free written estimate after a (video) survey. Instant quotes are fine as a first step if labeled 'quote, not an estimate'.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Common copy claim 'moving is one of life's most stressful events' vs Holmes & Rahe (1967)
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Verified study wins: don't print it as a fact. 'Moving is a lot' as emotional copy is fine.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold GOLD-018 bundle price table vs C-3PO one-job-per-piece and Bertrand (fewer options convert better)
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Verified study wins over vendor sample: show one hero price (or two options max) with what's included.
